question: How many types of taxes were in the reign of the ruler Alauddin Khalji?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296-1316), the second ruler of the Khalji dynasty, introduced major agrarian and market-control reforms to fund his large standing army. (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी — तीन प्रकार के कर)

 

• He imposed three main taxes: Kharaj (land revenue, fixed at about 50% of the produce), Charai (grazing tax on cattle), and Ghari (house tax).

 

• These reforms were part of his broader agrarian and market-control policies, administered through officials responsible for revenue assessment and collection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alauddin Khalji is also remembered for his strict market control policy, fixing prices of essential commodities, and for repelling repeated Mongol invasions.

 

• He built the Alai Darwaza at the Qutub complex and founded the city of Siri, his second capital in Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 2): Incorrect; Alauddin Khalji's revenue system is standardly counted as three taxes, not five.

 

• 6 (Option 3): Incorrect; this overstates the number of distinct taxes recognised in his agrarian reforms.

 

• 2 (Option 4): Incorrect; this understates the number — Kharaj, Charai and Ghari together make three, not two.

question: The bare ground between plants is covered with a layer of organic matter in order to retain soil moisture. This method is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mulching.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mulching is an agricultural practice in which the bare soil around plants is covered with a layer of organic or inorganic material (straw, dry leaves, plastic sheets, etc.) to conserve soil moisture. (मल्चिंग — मृदा नमी संरक्षण)

 

• It reduces evaporation of water from the soil surface, suppresses weed growth, moderates soil temperature, and improves soil fertility as organic mulch decomposes.

 

• Common mulch materials include straw, dry leaves, grass clippings, compost, and plastic films, used widely in horticulture and dryland farming.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Drip irrigation is often combined with mulching to maximise water-use efficiency in water-scarce regions.

 

• Mulching is a key technique of dryland/rainfed farming and soil and water conservation.

 

NOTE

 

• Rock dam (Option 2): A small check structure built across a gully or stream using stones to slow water flow and reduce soil erosion, not related to covering bare ground with organic matter.

 

• Shelter belts (Option 3): Rows of trees planted to reduce wind velocity and protect fields from wind erosion, not a ground-covering technique.

 

• Contour barriers (Option 4): Stone, grass, or soil barriers built along the contour of sloped land to reduce runoff and soil erosion, distinct from mulching.

question: In which of the following years was the Fit India Movement launched by Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, GoI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2019.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fit India Movement was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 29 August 2019 (National Sports Day, the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand), under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. (फिट इंडिया मूवमेंट — 29 अगस्त 2019)

 

• Its objective is to encourage citizens to incorporate physical activity and sports into their daily lives and bring about a behavioural change towards fitness.

 

• It was launched at the Indira Gandhi Stadium, New Delhi, and is run through the Fit India Movement Secretariat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Sports Day (29 August) also marks the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand, the legendary hockey player.

 

• Related government initiatives include Khelo India, launched in 2018 to promote grassroots sports.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (2018, 2001, 2020): All incorrect; the Fit India Movement was launched specifically in 2019, not in any of these years.

question: Husk of a coconut is made of ______ tissue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Scherenchyma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The husk (outer fibrous covering) of a coconut is made up of sclerenchyma tissue (printed in the source as "Scherenchyma"). (स्केलेरेंकाइमा ऊतक — नारियल की जटा)

 

• Sclerenchyma is a simple permanent tissue composed of dead cells with thick, lignified walls, providing mechanical strength and rigidity to plant parts.

 

• The tough, fibrous coir obtained from coconut husk (used to make ropes, mats and brushes) is composed of these sclerenchymatous fibres.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sclerenchyma fibres are also found in the stems of jute, hemp and flax, giving these plants their characteristic fibre strength.

 

• Sclerenchyma cells lack living protoplasm at maturity, unlike the living cells of parenchyma and collenchyma.

 

NOTE

 

• Collenchyma (Option 1): A living, flexible supporting tissue found in the growing parts of stems and leaf petioles, not in the hard coconut husk.

 

• Xylem (Option 2): A complex, water-conducting vascular tissue, not the tissue that forms the fibrous husk.

 

• Parenchyma (Option 4): A living, thin-walled packing/storage tissue, unlike the tough, dead-celled sclerenchyma of the husk.

question: Which of the following options is NOT correct about plant cells?
option_1: Cell wall of a plant cell is made up of cellulose.
option_2: The plant cells cannot divide by mitosis.
option_3: A plant cell usually contains a large vacuole.
option_4: Generally, all plant cells contain chloroplast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The plant cells cannot divide by mitosis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is NOT correct — plant cells, like most eukaryotic cells, can and do divide by mitosis; it is the primary mode of cell division responsible for growth in plants. (माइटोसिस विभाजन — पादप कोशिका)

 

• Mitosis in plant cells occurs mainly in meristematic tissues (apical, lateral and intercalary meristems), producing two genetically identical daughter cells.

 

• The other three statements are factually correct descriptions of plant cells: the cell wall is made of cellulose, plant cells usually have a large central vacuole, and most plant cells contain chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant cell division differs from animal cell division mainly in cytokinesis, where a cell plate forms to divide the cytoplasm, rather than the membrane constriction seen in animal cells.

 

• Meristematic cells are the actively dividing cells responsible for a plant's continuous growth throughout its life.

 

NOTE

 

• Cell wall made of cellulose (Option 1): A true statement about plant cells, so it is not the answer to this 'NOT correct' question.

 

• Large vacuole (Option 3): A true statement — plant cells typically have a large central vacuole for turgor pressure and storage, so it is not the answer.

 

• Chloroplast (Option 4): Generally true for photosynthetic plant cells as a textbook generalisation, so it is not the intended answer here.

question: The Government of India started DACE scheme in April 2022. This scheme was launched under which of the following ministries?
option_1: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dr. Ambedkar Centre of Excellence (DACE) scheme was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, in April 2022. (डॉ. अम्बेडकर उत्कृष्टता केंद्र — सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय)

 

• It was inaugurated by Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, with the Governor of UP, Anandiben Patel, in attendance.

 

• The scheme aims to provide quality free coaching to students from Scheduled Castes (SC) for entry into premier higher educational institutions and for competitive examinations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme is implemented through select universities/institutions notified as DACE centres across India.

 

• The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment also runs other SC welfare schemes such as the Post-Matric Scholarship and PM-AJAY.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Option 2): Deals with company law and corporate governance, unrelated to the DACE scheme.

 

• Ministry of Rural Development (Option 3): Handles rural welfare schemes like MGNREGA and PMAY-G, not DACE.

 

• Ministry of Education (Option 4): Oversees the general education system but did not launch the DACE scheme; it was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

question: Whose birthday is celebrated as International Day of Non-Violence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October every year, marking the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — महात्मा गांधी)

 

• It was established by the United Nations General Assembly in June 2007 to disseminate the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.

 

• Gandhi, the leader of India's freedom movement, pioneered the philosophy of Satyagraha (non-violent civil resistance), which inspired civil rights movements worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi is honoured with the title 'Father of the Nation' in India; his birthday, 2 October, is also a national holiday (Gandhi Jayanti).

 

• 2 October is additionally observed as the birth anniversary of Lal Bahadur Shastri, India's second Prime Minister.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 1): First President of independent India; his birthday is not associated with this UN observance.

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose (Option 2): Leader of the Indian National Army; his birthday (23 January) is observed as Parakram Diwas, not the International Day of Non-Violence.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 3): First Prime Minister of India; his birthday (14 November) is observed as Children's Day (Bal Diwas) in India.

question: Which of the following Indian freedom fighters said, "Be the change that you wish to see in the world"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The saying "Be the change that you wish to see in the world" is popularly attributed to Mahatma Gandhi, and it reflects his philosophy that individual self-transformation must precede social transformation. (महात्मा गांधी — प्रसिद्ध कथन)

 

• This idea is closely tied to his broader teachings on Satyagraha (truth-force/non-violent resistance) and Swaraj (self-rule), which emphasised personal conduct as the foundation of larger reform.

 

• As per the officially marked answer key of this exam, Mahatma Gandhi is the intended attribution among the given freedom fighters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi led major movements including the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and Quit India Movement (1942).

 

• He is widely referred to as 'Bapu' and 'Mahatma' (Great Soul).

 

NOTE

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 1): One of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio of extremist nationalist leaders, known for his role in the Swadeshi Movement, not associated with this quote.

 

• Mohammad Ali Jinnah (Option 2): Founder of Pakistan and leader of the All India Muslim League, not associated with this quote.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 3): Founder of the Indian National Association and a moderate Congress leader, not associated with this quote.

question: In which year was Kalidas Samman established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1980.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kalidas Samman was instituted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980 to honour excellence in classical and contemporary Indian arts. (कालिदास सम्मान — मध्य प्रदेश सरकार, 1980)

 

• It is awarded annually in four categories — classical music, classical dance, theatre, and plastic arts (sculpture/painting) — on a rotational basis.

 

• It is named after the great Sanskrit poet-dramatist Kalidasa, celebrated for works like Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Madhya Pradesh government also confers other prestigious honours such as the Tansen Samman (Hindustani classical music) and Lata Mangeshkar Puraskar.

 

• The award is traditionally presented at Ujjain, a city closely associated with Kalidasa's legendary life.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (1978, 1975, 1984): All incorrect; the Kalidas Samman was instituted specifically in 1980, not in any of these years.

question: Who among the following has won Oscars as well as a Golden Globe award for his contribution to international music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A.R.Rahman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A. R. Rahman, the celebrated Indian music composer, has won both an Academy Award (Oscar) and a Golden Globe Award for his work on the film Slumdog Millionaire (2008). (ए.आर. रहमान — ऑस्कर और गोल्डन ग्लोब विजेता)

 

• He won the Oscar for Best Original Score and Best Original Song ('Jai Ho'), and the Golden Globe for Best Original Score, both in 2009.

 

• He has also won two Grammy Awards and numerous National Film Awards and Filmfare Awards in India, and is often referred to as the 'Mozart of Madras'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A. R. Rahman's other notable scores include Roja, Bombay, Lagaan, Rockstar, and 127 Hours.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2010) by the Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Pt. Jasraj (Option 1): A legendary Hindustani classical vocalist, recipient of the Padma Vibhushan, but not a recipient of an Oscar or Golden Globe.

 

• Ravi Shankar (Option 3): A renowned sitar maestro who received Grammy Awards and an honorary Oscar nomination for 'Gandhi' (1982), but did not win a competitive Oscar or a Golden Globe.

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 4): A celebrated tabla virtuoso and Grammy winner, but not a recipient of an Oscar or Golden Globe.

question: Asia is separated from Europe by ______ mountains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ural.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asia and Europe together form the landmass known as Eurasia; the conventional physical boundary between them is the Ural Mountains, together with the Ural River and the Caucasus Mountains. (यूराल पर्वत — एशिया-यूरोप विभाजक)

 

• The Ural Mountains run roughly north-south through Russia, stretching about 2,500 km from the Arctic Ocean to the Kazakhstan border.

 

• This range is also historically significant for its mineral wealth, including iron ore, copper, and precious stones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Caucasus Mountains, between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea, form the southern part of the Asia-Europe boundary.

 

• Mount Elbrus, in the Caucasus, is often cited as Europe's highest peak.

 

NOTE

 

• Himalayan (Option 1): Separates the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau, entirely within Asia, not the Asia-Europe boundary.

 

• Andes Mountains (Option 2): The longest mountain range in the world, located in South America, unrelated to the Asia-Europe boundary.

 

• Alps (Option 3): Located entirely within Europe, forming a boundary between several European countries, not between Asia and Europe.

question: Which of the following states have the highest literacy rate, according to census 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states, at approximately 93.91%. (केरल — सर्वाधिक साक्षरता दर)

 

• Kerala has consistently topped literacy rankings due to sustained investment in public education, health, and social reform since the 19th century.

 

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep recorded a higher literacy rate than any state, but since it is a UT and not a state, Kerala holds the top position among states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate among states in the 2011 Census.

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (82.14% for males, 65.46% for females).

 

NOTE

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 1): A Union Territory, not a state; while it recorded a very high literacy rate, it is excluded from a state-wise comparison.

 

• Goa (Option 2): Has a high literacy rate but ranks below Kerala among Indian states.

 

• Mizoram (Option 3): Also has a high literacy rate (second among states) but ranks below Kerala.

question: The system based on individual leadership is a __________ system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is presidential.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A presidential system of government is one based on individual leadership, where the President is both the head of state and head of government, elected independently of the legislature. (राष्ट्रपति प्रणाली — व्यक्तिगत नेतृत्व)

 

• In this system there is a clear separation of powers between the executive and legislative branches, and the President is not accountable to the legislature for their continuance in office (e.g., the United States).

 

• This contrasts with a parliamentary system, where executive power lies with a Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the legislature, representing collective rather than individual leadership.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a parliamentary system of government, adapted from the British (Westminster) model, at both the Union and State levels.

 

• Countries like France follow a semi-presidential (hybrid) system, combining a directly elected President with a Prime Minister responsible to parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• Semi-parliamentary (Option 1): A hybrid system with features of both parliamentary and presidential systems, not based purely on individual leadership.

 

• Parliamentary (Option 2): Based on the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the legislature, not individual leadership.

 

• Semi-presidential (Option 4): Combines an elected president with a prime minister accountable to parliament, blending individual and collective leadership rather than being purely individual.

question: Which of the following rivers is NOT included in the ‘Panchnad’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Indus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Panchnad' literally means 'the land/confluence of five rivers', referring to the five tributaries of the Indus system in the Punjab region: the Beas, Sutlej, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum. (पंचनद — पंजाब की पाँच नदियाँ)

 

• These five rivers converge near Mithankot in Pakistan and eventually merge into the Indus River, which is the trunk river, not one of the five 'Panchnad' rivers itself.

 

• The name 'Punjab' (from Persian panj-ab, 'five waters') is directly derived from this same set of five rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indus River originates near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through Ladakh and Pakistan before draining into the Arabian Sea.

 

• The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) between India and Pakistan governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus and its tributaries, including the Panchnad rivers.

 

NOTE

 

• The Beas (Option 1): One of the five rivers that constitute the Panchnad, so it is correctly included.

 

• The Sutlej (Option 2): One of the five rivers of the Panchnad, so it is correctly included.

 

• The Ravi (Option 4): One of the five rivers of the Panchnad, so it is correctly included.

question: The final of the French Open (Roland Garros) Tennis 2021 for men took place on which day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 June.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2021 French Open (Roland Garros) men's singles final was played on 13 June 2021, in which Novak Djokovic defeated Stefanos Tsitsipas in five sets to win his second French Open and 19th Grand Slam title. (फ्रेंच ओपन 2021 — नोवाक जोकोविच)

 

• The tournament is held annually at the Stade Roland Garros in Paris, France, on clay courts, and is one of the four Grand Slam tennis tournaments.

 

• The 2021 women's singles title was won by Barbora Krejčíková, who defeated Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.

 

• Rafael Nadal holds the record for the most French Open men's singles titles.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (30 July, 13 July, 5 June): All incorrect dates; the actual men's final of the 2021 French Open was played on 13 June 2021.

question: Union Minister of Petroleum & Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri inaugurated Asia’s largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri inaugurated Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant, set up by Verbio India, at Lehragaga in Sangrur district, Punjab. (एशिया का सबसे बड़ा सीबीजी संयंत्र — पंजाब)

 

• The plant converts paddy straw (stubble) into compressed bio gas, helping curb the practice of stubble burning while generating clean fuel and organic manure.

 

• It is part of the Government of India's SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) scheme, which promotes CBG plants across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• SATAT was launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to set up CBG production plants and market CBG as a green transport fuel.

 

• CBG plants help reduce air pollution from stubble burning, a major contributor to winter smog in North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Not the location of this particular Asia's-largest CBG plant.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Not the location of this plant.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Not the location of this plant; the plant is located in Punjab.

question: Identify the correct statement with respect to unsaturated hydrocarbons.
option_1: Compounds of carbon having a single bond between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
option_2: Compounds of carbon having double bonds or triple bonds between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
option_3: Compounds of carbon having single bonds between their oxygen atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
option_4: Compounds of carbon having double or triple bonds between their hydrogen atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Compounds of carbon having double bonds or triple bonds between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons are compounds of carbon and hydrogen containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond (alkenes) or triple bond (alkynes). (असंतृप्त हाइड्रोकार्बन — द्विआबंध/त्रिआबंध)

 

• Because of these multiple bonds, unsaturated hydrocarbons are more reactive than saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) and readily undergo addition reactions (e.g., with hydrogen, halogens).

 

• Examples include ethene (C₂H₄), which has a carbon-carbon double bond, and ethyne (C₂H₂), which has a carbon-carbon triple bond.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), like methane and ethane, contain only single (C-C) bonds and are relatively less reactive, undergoing mainly substitution reactions.

 

• The general formulas are CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes and CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ for alkynes.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect; a single bond between carbon atoms characterises saturated (not unsaturated) compounds.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect; unsaturation is defined by bonding between carbon atoms, not oxygen atoms, and single bonds do not indicate unsaturation.

 

• Option 4: Incorrect; unsaturation refers to multiple bonds between carbon atoms, not between hydrogen atoms (hydrogen atoms do not bond to each other within a hydrocarbon chain).

question: Some important administrative posts were hereditary during the Rashtrakuta and Chola dynasties. The post ‘nagara-shreshthi’ meant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Merchant of the city.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the Rashtrakuta and Chola periods, several administrative and guild-related posts were hereditary; 'nagara-shreshthi' referred to the chief merchant (head of the merchant community) of a city/town. (नगर-श्रेष्ठी — नगर का प्रमुख व्यापारी)

 

• The nagara-shreshthi played an important role in urban administration, often serving alongside other local officials in managing trade, guilds (shrenis), and civic affairs.

 

• Such hereditary posts reflect the importance of merchant guilds in South Indian urban and economic administration during this period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola administration was noted for its well-organised local self-government, including village assemblies like the Ur and Sabha.

 

• Trade guilds such as the Manigramam and Ayyavole (Aihole 500) were prominent merchant organisations of medieval South India.

 

NOTE

 

• Leader of the merchant caravans (Option 1): This role is generally associated with titles like 'Sarthavaha', not 'nagara-shreshthi'.

 

• Important minister (Option 3): Ministerial posts had different designations (e.g., 'Sandhivigrahika', 'Mahasandhivigrahika'), distinct from 'nagara-shreshthi'.

 

• Chief judicial officer (Option 4): Judicial functions were carried out by different designated officials, not the 'nagara-shreshthi', whose role was specifically related to trade and merchants.

question: Which of the following is added in the national income to obtain personal income of the households?
option_2: Transfer payments from government and firms
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transfer payments from government and firms.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Personal Income is derived from National Income by subtracting incomes earned but not received by households and adding incomes received but not currently earned. (व्यक्तिगत आय — हस्तांतरण भुगतान जोड़ना)

 

• To move from National Income to Personal Income: subtract corporate/undistributed profits, corporate (profit) taxes, and net interest payments made by businesses; then add transfer payments (like pensions, scholarships, subsidies) received by households from the government and firms, which are received but not earned through current productive activity.

 

• Transfer payments are thus added because households receive this income without corresponding current production, making them part of personal income even though they are excluded from national income.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Personal Disposable Income is obtained by further subtracting direct personal taxes from Personal Income.

 

• National income accounting distinguishes between factor income (earned through production) and transfer income (received without corresponding production).

 

NOTE

 

• Net interest payments (Option 1): Typically subtracted (as interest paid by businesses/government), not added, when moving from national income to personal income.

 

• Undistributed profits (Option 3): Corporate profits retained by firms and not distributed to households, so they are subtracted, not added.

 

• Corporate tax (Option 4): The tax paid by companies on profits; it is subtracted when calculating personal income, as it is not received by households.

question: Who conducted X-ray spectroscopic study of a large number of elements and showed that the frequency of X-rays emitted by an element is related to the atomic number, Z, rather than the atomic mass?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Moseley.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Moseley, a British physicist, conducted X-ray spectroscopic studies of a large number of elements in 1913 and discovered that the frequency of characteristic X-rays emitted by an element is related to its atomic number (Z), not its atomic mass. (हेनरी मोसले — परमाणु क्रमांक)

 

• This discovery, known as Moseley's Law, provided the physical basis for arranging elements by atomic number rather than atomic mass, resolving earlier anomalies in Mendeleev's periodic table.

 

• Moseley's work directly led to the modern statement of the Periodic Law: the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev formulated the original Periodic Table based on atomic mass in 1869, leaving gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

• Johann Döbereiner proposed the 'Law of Triads', and Lothar Meyer independently worked on atomic-volume-based periodicity around the same time as Mendeleev.

 

NOTE

 

• Lothar Meyer (Option 1): Worked on periodicity based on atomic volume, not X-ray spectroscopy or atomic number.

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev (Option 2): Arranged elements by atomic mass in the original periodic table, not atomic number, and did not use X-ray spectroscopy.

 

• Johann Dobereiner (Option 4): Proposed the Law of Triads, an early classification of elements, unrelated to X-ray spectroscopy or atomic number.

question: Which Five-Year Plan in India was mainly focussed on Garibi Hatao, creation of employment opportunities and agricultural production amongst other objectives?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979) of India had 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty) and self-reliance as its central objectives, along with employment generation and growth in agricultural production. (गरीबी हटाओ — पाँचवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना)

 

• The slogan 'Garibi Hatao' was popularised by Indira Gandhi in her 1971 election campaign, and became the guiding theme incorporated into the Fifth Plan's objectives.

 

• The plan also emphasised employment and justice, though it was terminated one year early, in 1978, by the Janata Government, which introduced a rolling plan instead.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) focused on the objectives of 'Growth with Stability' and progress towards self-reliance.

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Plan (2012-2017).

 

NOTE

 

• Fourth (Option 2): Focused on growth with stability, not specifically on Garibi Hatao.

 

• Third (Option 3): Aimed to make the economy self-reliant, but its implementation was disrupted by the Indo-China (1962) and Indo-Pak (1965) wars and drought.

 

• Second (Option 4): Based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasising rapid industrialisation and heavy industries, not Garibi Hatao.

question: What are the two most essential rights of democracy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equality, freedom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Equality (समानता) and Freedom/Liberty (स्वतंत्रता) are widely regarded as the two most essential and foundational rights underpinning a democratic system. (समानता, स्वतंत्रता — लोकतंत्र के दो आवश्यक अधिकार)

 

• Freedom ensures citizens can exercise personal, political and civil liberties, such as freedom of speech, expression, movement, and association.

 

• Equality ensures all citizens are treated alike before the law, with equal access to opportunities, and is enshrined in India through Articles 14-18 of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights (Part III), including the Right to Equality and Right to Freedom, as essential democratic guarantees.

 

• Preventive detention, by contrast, is a restrictive/exceptional power (Article 22) allowing the state to detain a person without trial, and is not itself a democratic 'right' but a limitation on liberty.

 

NOTE

 

• Exploitation, preventive detention (Option 1): Neither represents a core democratic right; exploitation is what rights protect against, and preventive detention is a restriction, not a right.

 

• Freedom, preventive detention (Option 3): While freedom is correct, preventive detention is a state power/restriction, not one of the two essential democratic rights.

 

• Equality, exploitation (Option 4): While equality is correct, exploitation is something rights protect against, not itself an essential right of democracy.

question: In March 2022, the “Stree Manoraksha project” was launched by which of the following Union Minister?
option_2: Union Minister for Women and Child Development
option_3: Union Minister for Law and Justice
option_4: Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Minister for Women and Child Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Stree Manoraksha Project' was launched in March 2022 by Smriti Zubin Irani, the Union Minister for Women and Child Development. (स्त्री मनोरक्षा परियोजना — महिला एवं बाल विकास मंत्री)

 

• The project focuses on capacity building for the psychosocial care and protection of women, particularly those in vulnerable circumstances such as institutional care.

 

• It was launched in collaboration with organisations working on mental health and gender-sensitive psychosocial support systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Women and Child Development also runs schemes such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Mission Shakti, and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

 

• Smriti Irani has also held the portfolio of the Ministry of Minority Affairs in the past.

 

NOTE

 

• Union Minister for Education (Option 1): Not associated with the launch of the Stree Manoraksha Project.

 

• Union Minister for Law and Justice (Option 3): Not associated with the launch of this project.

 

• Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare (Option 4): Not associated with the launch of this project; it was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

question: Jata-Jatin is the folk dance of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jata-Jatin is a traditional folk dance of Bihar, performed by both men and women, typically during the rainy season, often associated with themes of love, separation and rural life. (जटा-जटिन — बिहार का लोकनृत्य)

 

• The dance is usually accompanied by folk songs narrating stories of a couple named 'Jata' and 'Jatin', performed in a simple rural style with rhythmic movements.

 

• It reflects the agrarian and cultural traditions of the Mithila and Bhojpur regions of Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Bihar include Jhijhian, Kajari, and Domkach.

 

• Bihar is also known for its classical art forms like Madhubani (Mithila) painting.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for classical dances like Raas Lila and folk dances such as Thang-Ta and Pung Cholom, not Jata-Jatin.

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for Odissi (classical) and folk dances like Chhau and Gotipua, not Jata-Jatin.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Known for folk dances such as Chhau, Baul, and Gambhira, not Jata-Jatin.

question: Mughal ruler, Aurangzeb died in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1707.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, died on 3 March 1707 at Ahmednagar, in present-day Maharashtra, after a reign of nearly 49 years. (औरंगजेब — मृत्यु 1707)

 

• His death marked the beginning of the decline of the Mughal Empire, followed by a war of succession among his sons and the eventual rise of regional powers.

 

• Aurangzeb was known for his campaigns of territorial expansion into the Deccan and for reversing several of Akbar's policies of religious tolerance, including the reimposition of the Jizya tax.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aurangzeb was succeeded, after a war of succession, by his son Bahadur Shah I.

 

• Aurangzeb's long Deccan campaigns against the Marathas (under Shivaji and his successors) drained the Mughal treasury and military strength.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (1703, 1705, 1701): All incorrect; Aurangzeb died specifically in 1707, not in any of these years.
